habitat: Singly or in pairs in dense vegetation over water, mostly in the lower layer. Secretive.
summary: A common resident. Dark brown above, with a broad rounded tail, a clear eye-stripe, and faint markings on the upper breast. The call is a loud accelerating 'cruk, cruk, cruk', like a stick drawn across a railing, followed by wing-snapping. The Kemp name African Sedge Warbler and the code RB were left unchanged.

underparts.pattern: Faint markings on the upper breast.

viewNotes.note: Dark brown above, with an eye-stripe and a broad rounded tail.
Faint markings on the upper breast.
Flight plumage is not described. The call is followed by wing-snapping.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A loud accelerating 'cruk, cruk, cruk, cruk-cruk-cruk', like a stick drawn across a railing, followed by wing-snapping. The grade A call is from Grahamstown. The filename is XC397750-Little Rush Warbler30 dec belmont.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. No Kruger photograph was found. The grade A call is from the Eastern Cape. The Kemp name African Sedge Warbler and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.
